### What does this PR do?

The trainer-side exporter and rollout engine can interpret the same quantization configuration differently, silently sending quantized bytes into a BF16 parameter or the reverse. This PR audits training versus export and export versus the receiving engine, reporting which weights disagree. When the vLLM audit raises, it finishes the bucket acknowledgements before surfacing the error so the trainer is not stranded waiting for an acknowledgement.

This is the standalone quantized-layer audit split of the closed #8327, prepared from [fork PR #8](https://github.com/wengeezhang/verl/pull/8). It targets current `main` directly, without the sentinel in #8495 or the separate post-sync self-check. The original fork branch is preserved.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [#8327 references](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+8327+in%3Abody), [quant audit](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+quant+audit), and [weight check](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+weight+check). No open PR implements these two audit boundaries. #8495 observes training metrics; #8486 checks repeatability of startup weight loads, not whether training/export/receiver agree on which layers are quantized. #8110 changes VeOmni exports to verified receiver dtypes for its unquantized BF16 path; this PR diagnoses format disagreement in quantized rollout and does not change exporter casting policy.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

On this standalone branch, based on main `2bcc98a9b64bdb3af5b88ac870ba0709ed709aef`:

- **55 CPU tests passed** using PyTorch 2.9.1 and Python 3.12: training traces and offload retention, export/receiver matching for both engines, first-sync lifecycle, warn/raise/off modes, and vLLM acknowledgement draining after a bucket error. Historical #8327 tests were copied outside the checkout and pointed at this branch; SGLang audit cases were separated from the independent self-check cases.
- The run includes two additional temporary checks executing the production audit-installation block with and without an engine's TE audit interface. Both preserve exporter installation; engines without that interface no longer receive an unsupported method call.
- All pre-commit hooks passed on the changed files; `git diff --check` passed.

Commands run (the external test directory is a local validation artifact, not committed CI coverage):

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" python -m pytest /tmp/verl-split-official-submit/audit-tests -q --disable-warnings --maxfail=2
pre-commit run --files $(git diff 2bcc98a9b64bdb3af5b88ac870ba0709ed709aef --name-only) --show-diff-on-failure
```

**Historical hardware evidence, not rerun on this rebased branch:** [fork PR #8](https://github.com/wengeezhang/verl/pull/8) records 1×B200, tiny Qwen3-MoE, two GRPO steps with vLLM 0.29.0 / SGLang 0.5.20, Transformer Engine 2.16.1 and Megatron-Core 0.19.2. Both engines checked 69 weights with zero mismatches or unmapped names; the training comparison agreed after step 1. BF16 training kept the receiver audit active. Injecting BF16 `o_proj` into an FP8 receiver named the offending weight and failed before its bucket was written. Before the acknowledgement fix, vLLM hung; afterward the run failed about five seconds after the report. Earlier 4×B200 Qwen3-30B-A3B validation checked 48 decoder layers and 18,867 received weights.

Current main pins vLLM 0.32.0. Local CPU tests use engine stand-ins and do not replace a fresh GPU run on that dependency version. Fresh B200 validation remains outstanding.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
# Default is warn: report disagreement and continue.
export VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT=raise
# Optional training-side diagnostic logging:
export VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT_TRACE=1
# VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT=0 disables both comparisons.
```

Training versus export runs once after TE FP8 workspace evidence becomes available. Export versus engine runs on every bucket of the first completed sync, before writing each bucket. These checks classify high-precision versus quantized weights; they do not prove identical quantization scales, numerical formats or kernel outputs. Unresolved engine names are counted as unjudged.

### Design & Code Changes

- `TrainExportAudit` compares each decoder layer's TE FP8 workspace evidence with exported GEMM projections. Offload remembers workspace evidence before clearing the cache. The comparison is per decoder layer, not individual TE operation; absent workspace evidence produces a warning instead of a fabricated verdict.
- `SyncFormatCheck` shares the receiver-side comparison across vLLM and SGLang, with engine-specific resolution of fused projections and expert parameters. SGLang coverage follows current main's MXFP8/MXFP4 custom refit loader; it does not cover FP8_BLOCK or claim removed NVFP4 support.
- vLLM catches bucket-loading exceptions, acknowledges and discards subsequent buckets, then re-raises the original exception after the sender finishes. This prevents a local loading/audit error from hanging the sender; it does not recover a partially written model.
- The training-side audit is installed only when the training engine exposes `set_train_export_audit`, preserving current main's VeOmni exporter support. Receiver checks remain independent of the training backend.
- Documentation lives in `docs/low_precision/qat.md`; no dependency on sentinel or self-check documentation/code is introduced.

AI assistance was used for the original implementation and for this standalone port, conflict resolution and CPU validation with Codex. The original human review and hardware validation are recorded in fork PR #8; the main-port adjustments and outstanding GPU validation are identified above for review.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Apply the full-repository pre-commit command from the template. All hooks were run successfully on the changed files; `--all-files` was not run.
- [x] Update the documentation.
- [ ] Add unit or end-to-end tests to CI. The split intentionally retains the original decision to omit new test files; the external CPU regression run and historical hardware evidence above are not a claim of added CI coverage.
- [ ] Request CI in the community channel. Not sent from this submission.
- [ ] Update the recipe submodule. Not applicable.

@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
 # Low-Precision Rollout and Quantization-Aware Training
 
-Last updated: 11/2/2026
+Last updated: 11/03/2026
 
 In RL training, rollout usually dominates the step time, and for large MoE models it is bound by memory capacity and bandwidth. Running rollout in low precision:
 
@@ -275,6 +275,33 @@ SGLang uses the default CUDA Graph configuration):
 | Blackwell | vLLM | ❌ | NVFP4 MoE | FlashInfer TRT-LLM (MoE; BF16 Linear) | 0.00966 |
 | Blackwell | vLLM | ❌ | NVFP4 MoE + NVFP4 QAT | FlashInfer TRT-LLM (MoE; BF16 Linear) | 0.00766 |
 
+## Quantized-layer audit
+
+Three parties decide which layers are quantized, each on its own: training implicitly (TE linear modules
+inside `fp8_autocast`), and by name the trainer-side exporter and the engine, both from the same quantization
+config (`rollout.quantization`, or the checkpoint's own `quantization_config`). The audit compares them in two
+steps, each once:
+
+- **Training vs export**, when Megatron training runs a TE FP8 recipe, at the first weight sync after a training step
+  (the sync before it has no FP8 trace yet): each decoder layer's FP8 trace (TE's FP8 weight workspaces)
+  against the format the sync sends for that layer's GEMM projections (attention, MLP, experts,
+  linear-attention and SSM in / out projections). Weights the exporter keeps in BF16 by design are skipped.
+  Other decoder-layer weights, such as a convolution, are not judged, and the audit reports how many it left
+  out.
+- **Export vs engine**, whenever the rollout is quantized, during the first weight sync: inside the engine's
+  weight loader, before each bucket is written, every incoming weight's format (quantized or high
+  precision) against the engine parameter that receives it. vLLM checks every quantized format; SGLang
+  checks the formats of its refit loader (MXFP8, MXFP4). Later syncs send the same formats and are
+  not checked again.
+

+"""Training vs export: did training run each decoder layer in the format the weight sync sends it in?
+
+This is the training half of the quantized-layer audit. The rollout half, export vs engine, runs inside each
+rollout engine's weight loader (``verl.utils.quant_sync_format_check``); ``VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT`` switches both.
+
+Why. Matched train/rollout quantization presumes both sides quantize the same
+layers, but each side decides on its own: training implicitly (a layer runs FP8
+GEMMs iff its TE linear modules run inside ``fp8_autocast``: the decoder layers,
+minus ``first_last_layers_bf16``; never the embedding, the mcore output layer or
+the torch-implemented MoE router), rollout by name (the trainer-side exporter
+from ``rollout.quantization``, the engine from the configuration it was started
+with). On B200, vLLM 0.24's ModelOpt MXFP8 config matched the router exclusion
+``mlp.gate`` as a prefix of the dense ``mlp.gate_up_proj``: 56 of 311 parameters
+of Qwen3-1.7B were served in BF16 while training ran them in FP8, and nothing
+reported it. There training and the export agreed and the engine did not, which
+is the rollout half's to catch; this module covers the training side.
+
+What. Two sources:
+
+- training: which decoder layers hold a TE FP8 weight workspace
+  (``module._fp8_workspaces``), per mcore ``TransformerLayer``;
+- export: what the sync actually sends, read from the trainer's weight stream
+  after the rollout weight quantizer (``dispatch_rollout_weight_quantizer``): a
+  quantized weight arrives in FP8 (or packed FP4, as ``weight_packed``), every
+  other weight in high precision.
+
+The comparison skips the modules the exporter keeps in BF16 by design (its
+``DEFAULT_IGNORE``: ``lm_head``, embeddings, vision towers, MTP layers, routers,
+the shared-expert gate) and judges the GEMM projections of each decoder layer
+(attention, MLP, experts, linear-attention / SSM in and out projections) against
+that layer's FP8 trace. A decoder-layer weight of any other kind, such as a
+convolution, is not judged, since the layer-level trace says nothing about it;
+the audit reports how many it left out.
+
+It runs once, when training runs a TE FP8 recipe and the rollout is quantized, at
+the first weight sync that happens after an FP8 forward (the first sync, before any
+step, has no workspaces yet). ``VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT``: ``warn`` (default) logs the
+disagreements, ``raise`` raises ``RuntimeError``, ``0`` disables.
+
+Two things can remove the training-side signal, and the audit says so instead of
+staying silent. verl drops the workspaces when it offloads the training model
+(``offload_megatron_model_to_cpu``, at the end of every ``train_mode()`` when
+``param_offload`` is on), so the clearing helper first marks every module that
+held one (``remember_fp8_workspaces``) and the audit accepts the marker. And TE
+only caches the FP8 weight when mcore passes ``is_first_microbatch``, which
+``disable_parameter_transpose_cache=True`` turns off; with that flag there is
+nothing to read, and the audit warns once that it cannot run.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import os
+import re
+import sys
+from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator, Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Optional

+import torch

+def _configure_audit_logger() -> logging.Logger:
+    """Route the audit's own output to stderr, past whatever the root logger was set to.
+
+    The audit's evidence lines are INFO/WARNING. Inside the trainer worker process a vLLM transitive
+    dependency (``model_hosting_container_standards.logging_config.configure_root_logger``, pulled in
+    for SageMaker) raises the root logger and every root handler to ERROR at import time; anything that
+    reaches this logger and then propagates to the root handlers is silently dropped - which is why the
+    audit was invisible on the first B200 runs even though it was executing. A dedicated stderr handler
+    on this logger with ``propagate=False`` carries the audit's INFO/WARNING lines out on their own,
+    independent of the root configuration.
+    """
+    log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+    log.setLevel(os.getenv("VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL", "INFO").upper())
+    log.propagate = False
+    handler_name = "verl.quant_audit.stderr"
+    if not any(getattr(h, "name", None) == handler_name for h in log.handlers):
+        handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr)
+        handler.set_name(handler_name)
+        handler.setLevel(logging.NOTSET)  # let the logger's own level decide
+        handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s %(levelname)s [quant-audit pid=%(process)d] %(message)s"))
+        log.addHandler(handler)
+    return log
+
+
+logger = _configure_audit_logger()
+
+_LAYER_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|\.)layers\.(\d+)\.")
+# Routers (and mcore's shared-expert gate) are plain torch linears on the training side, never TE,
+# regardless of how the HF checkpoint names them.
+_ROUTER_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|\.)(gate|router|shared_expert_gate)\.weight$")
+# Non-linear leaves inside a decoder layer that never see a TE GEMM.
+_NON_LINEAR_RE = re.compile(r"(norm|embed|rotary|bias$)", re.IGNORECASE)
+_FP8_DTYPES = (torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.float8_e5m2)
+# compressed-tensors' name for a packed FP4 weight; the module's ``weight`` in every other format.
+_PACKED_SUFFIX = ".weight_packed"
+_MAX_LISTED = 40
+
+
+def audit_mode() -> str:
+    return os.environ.get("VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT", "warn").strip().lower()
+
+
+def trace(where: str, **state) -> None:
+    """Log one checkpoint of the audit's own execution, at WARNING, when tracing is on.
+
+    A guard that produces nothing is impossible to diagnose from the outside: telling "never
+    installed" from "installed but never reached" from "reached but found nothing" otherwise needs
+    instrumented runs. ``VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT_TRACE=1`` makes each of those states visible in one
+    run, at a level no logging configuration drops.
+    """
+    if os.environ.get("VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT_TRACE", "0") != "1":
+        return
+    detail = " ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in state.items())
+    logger.warning("quantized-layer audit trace: %s%s", where, f" | {detail}" if detail else "")
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Training side: which decoder layers ran FP8 GEMMs
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@dataclass
+class TrainFp8Report:
+    """Which decoder layers ran FP8 GEMMs on this rank, read from TE's workspaces."""
+
+    seen_layers: set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
+    quantized_layers: set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
+    outside_layers_quantized: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    # mcore's TE wrappers carry config.disable_parameter_transpose_cache; True means TE never caches
+    # the FP8 weight (is_first_microbatch=None), so no workspace can ever appear.
+    transpose_cache_disabled: bool = False
+
+    @property
+    def active(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self.quantized_layers) or bool(self.outside_layers_quantized)
+
+
+def fp8_recipe_of(engine_config) -> Optional[str]:
+    """The Transformer Engine FP8 recipe a Megatron engine trains with, or None for BF16 GEMMs.
+
+    Read from ``override_transformer_config``, the keys the Megatron provider receives: ``fp8``
+    turns TE's FP8 GEMMs on and ``fp8_recipe`` picks the scaling recipe (Megatron's default is
+    ``delayed``). Engines without that config return None.
+    """
+    overrides = getattr(engine_config, "override_transformer_config", None)
+    if not overrides or not overrides.get("fp8"):
+        return None
+    return str(overrides.get("fp8_recipe") or "delayed").lower()
+
+
+# Set on a TE module whose FP8 weight workspace verl has dropped (param offload); survives the offload.
+FP8_WORKSPACE_SEEN_ATTR = "_verl_fp8_workspace_seen"
+
+
+def remember_fp8_workspaces(module: torch.nn.Module) -> bool:
+    """Mark ``module`` as having held an FP8 weight workspace. Call before clearing ``_fp8_workspaces``."""
+    ws = getattr(module, "_fp8_workspaces", None)
+    if isinstance(ws, dict) and len(ws) > 0:
+        setattr(module, FP8_WORKSPACE_SEEN_ATTR, True)
+        return True
+    return False
+
+
+def _has_fp8_workspace(module: torch.nn.Module) -> bool:
+    ws = getattr(module, "_fp8_workspaces", None)
+    return (isinstance(ws, dict) and len(ws) > 0) or bool(getattr(module, FP8_WORKSPACE_SEEN_ATTR, False))
+
+
+def _is_transformer_layer(module: torch.nn.Module) -> bool:
+    return isinstance(getattr(module, "layer_number", None), int) and "TransformerLayer" in type(module).__name__
+
+
+def collect_train_fp8_report(modules: Iterable[torch.nn.Module] | torch.nn.Module) -> TrainFp8Report:
+    """Walk Megatron model chunks and record, per global decoder layer, whether any TE module quantized."""
+    if isinstance(modules, torch.nn.Module):
+        modules = [modules]
+    report = TrainFp8Report()
+    for chunk in modules:
+        in_layer: set[int] = set()
+        for _, layer in chunk.named_modules():
+            if not _is_transformer_layer(layer):
+                continue
+            idx = layer.layer_number - 1  # mcore layer_number is 1-based and global across PP
+            report.seen_layers.add(idx)
+            for sub in layer.modules():
+                in_layer.add(id(sub))
+                if getattr(sub, "disable_parameter_transpose_cache", False):
+                    report.transpose_cache_disabled = True
+                if _has_fp8_workspace(sub):
+                    report.quantized_layers.add(idx)
+        for name, sub in chunk.named_modules():
+            if id(sub) not in in_layer and _has_fp8_workspace(sub):
+                report.outside_layers_quantized.append(name)
+    return report
+
+
+# transformers >= 5 saves MoE experts fused and without a ``.weight`` suffix
+# (``mlp.experts.gate_up_proj`` [E, 2I, H], ``mlp.experts.down_proj`` [E, H, I]).
+_FUSED_EXPERT_RE = re.compile(r"\.experts\.(gate_up_proj|down_proj)$")
+
+
+def is_linear_weight_name(name: str) -> bool:
+    return name.endswith(".weight") or bool(_FUSED_EXPERT_RE.search(name))
+
+
+# HF leaf modules of the projections a decoder layer runs as TE GEMMs: attention (including MLA), MLP,
+# experts (Mixtral's w1/w2/w3 too) and the in / out projections of linear-attention and SSM mixers.
+_GEMM_WEIGHT_RE = re.compile(
+    r"(?:^|\.)(?:q_proj|k_proj|v_proj|o_proj|qkv_proj|query_key_value|q_a_proj|q_b_proj|kv_a_proj_with_mqa|"
+    r"kv_b_proj|gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj|gate_up_proj|in_proj\w*|out_proj|fc1|fc2|w1|w2|w3)\.weight$"
+)
+
+
+def is_gemm_weight_name(name: str) -> bool:
+    return bool(_GEMM_WEIGHT_RE.search(name) or _FUSED_EXPERT_RE.search(name))
+
+
+def _of_unjudged_kind(name: str) -> bool:
+    """A decoder-layer weight that is neither a known GEMM projection nor a known non-GEMM leaf."""
+    return (
+        is_linear_weight_name(name)
+        and _LAYER_RE.search(name) is not None
+        and not (_ROUTER_RE.search(name) or _NON_LINEAR_RE.search(name))
+        and not is_gemm_weight_name(name)
+    )
+
+
+def expected_train_quantized(name: str, report: TrainFp8Report) -> Optional[bool]:
+    """Training-side expectation for one HF weight name; ``None`` when this rank cannot judge."""
+    if not is_linear_weight_name(name):
+        return False
+    m = _LAYER_RE.search(name)
+    if m is None:
+        # embeddings, lm_head, vision towers, ...: mcore quantizes nothing outside the decoder stack
+        return None if report.outside_layers_quantized else False
+    idx = int(m.group(1))
+    if idx not in report.seen_layers:
+        return None  # another pipeline stage owns this layer
+    if _ROUTER_RE.search(name) or _NON_LINEAR_RE.search(name):
+        return False
+    if not is_gemm_weight_name(name):
+        return None  # e.g. a convolution: the layer's FP8 trace does not say how training ran it
+    return idx in report.quantized_layers
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Export side: what the weight sync sends
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def exported_weight(name: str, tensor: torch.Tensor) -> Optional[tuple[str, bool, str]]:
+    """``(weight name, quantized, format)`` for one entry of the exported stream; ``None`` for scales and the rest."""
+    if name.endswith(_PACKED_SUFFIX):
+        return name[: -len("_packed")], True, "packed FP4"
+    if not is_linear_weight_name(name):
+        return None
+    dtype = getattr(tensor, "dtype", None)
+    return name, dtype in _FP8_DTYPES, str(dtype).removeprefix("torch.")
+
+
+def kept_high_precision_by_design(name: str) -> bool:
+    """Whether the exporter keeps this weight's module in BF16 whatever the preset (its ``DEFAULT_IGNORE``)."""
+    from verl.utils.qat.compressed_tensors import DEFAULT_IGNORE, _matches
+
+    module = name[: -len(".weight")] if name.endswith(".weight") else name
+    return _matches(module, DEFAULT_IGNORE)
+
+
+def unjudged_weights(exported: Mapping[str, tuple[bool, str]]) -> list[str]:
+    """Exported decoder-layer weights of a kind the training-vs-export comparison does not judge."""
+    return [name for name in exported if _of_unjudged_kind(name) and not kept_high_precision_by_design(name)]
+
+
+def _unjudged_note(unjudged: list[str]) -> str:
+    if not unjudged:
+        return ""
+    shown = ", ".join(unjudged[:3]) + (", ..." if len(unjudged) > 3 else "")
+    return f"; {len(unjudged)} decoder-layer weights of a kind the audit does not judge, e.g. {shown}"
+
+
+def audit_train_vs_export(report: TrainFp8Report, exported: Mapping[str, tuple[bool, str]]) -> tuple[list[str], int]:
+    """One line per exported weight on which training and the export disagree, and the by-design skip count."""
+    problems = []
+    by_design = 0
+    for name, (quantized, fmt) in exported.items():
+        if kept_high_precision_by_design(name):
+            by_design += 1
+            continue
+        expected = expected_train_quantized(name, report)
+        if expected is None:
+            continue
+        if quantized and not expected:
+            problems.append(f"{name}: the export sends it in {fmt}, training ran it in high precision")
+        elif expected and not quantized:
+            problems.append(f"{name}: training ran it in FP8, the export sends it in {fmt}")
+    return problems, by_design
+
+
+def _listing(problems: list[str]) -> str:
+    return (
+        "\n  - "
+        + "\n  - ".join(problems[:_MAX_LISTED])
+        + (f"\n  - ... and {len(problems) - _MAX_LISTED} more" if len(problems) > _MAX_LISTED else "")
+    )
+

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Training vs export, once per run
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+class TrainExportAudit:
+    """Training vs export: did training run each decoder layer in the format the weight sync sends it in?
+
+    ``wrap_export`` wraps the training engine's weight export after the rollout weight quantizer, the one
+    point every sync route passes through (the colocated worker, the checkpoint engine, server replicas):
+    it records the format of every exported weight and, when the stream ends, calls
+    ``compare_with_training``. The comparison needs TE's FP8 weight workspaces, which exist only after a
+    training step, so the sync before any step waits and the first sync after one decides; from then on
+    the export passes through untouched.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, mode: str, engine: str = "", enabled: bool = True):
+        self.mode = mode
+        self.engine = engine
+        self.enabled = enabled and mode not in ("0", "off", "false")
+        self.finished = False  # compared, or gave up for lack of a training-side FP8 trace
+        # HF weight name -> (sent quantized, format), from the last recorded sync
+        self.exported: dict[str, tuple[bool, str]] = {}
+        self.syncs_seen = 0  # distinct weight syncs wrapped; the give-up threshold counts these
+        self._explained = False  # one-shot "why this guard produced nothing" warning
+
+    @classmethod
+    def create(cls, *, rollout_quantized: bool, trainer_fp8_recipe: Optional[str], rollout_name: str):
+        """Arm the comparison for a TE FP8 trainer whose rollout is quantized; otherwise return a disabled audit."""
+        mode = audit_mode()
+        if not rollout_quantized or trainer_fp8_recipe is None:
+            logger.info(
+                "quantized-layer audit, training vs export: not armed (rollout quantized=%s, training FP8 recipe=%s): "
+                "no FP8 training to compare",
+                rollout_quantized,
+                trainer_fp8_recipe,
+            )
+            return cls(mode, rollout_name, enabled=False)
+        logger.info(
+            "quantized-layer audit, training vs export: armed (engine=%s, training FP8 recipe=%s, mode=%s); runs at "
+            "the first weight sync after a training step",
+            rollout_name,
+            trainer_fp8_recipe,
+            mode,
+        )
+        return cls(mode, rollout_name)
+
+    def wrap_export(
+        self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]], training_modules=None
+    ) -> Iterator[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]:
+        """Pass the exported stream through, recording each weight's format; compare with training when it ends.
+
+        ``training_modules`` (the Megatron model chunks) makes the comparison run as soon as the stream is
+        exhausted, wherever the stream is consumed.
+        """
+        trace("wrap_export", enabled=self.enabled, finished=self.finished, with_modules=training_modules is not None)
+        if not self.enabled or self.finished:
+            yield from weights
+            return
+        self.exported = {}
+        self.syncs_seen += 1  # one wrapped weight stream == one sync
+        for name, tensor in weights:
+            entry = exported_weight(name, tensor)
+            if entry is not None:
+                self.exported[entry[0]] = entry[1:]
+            yield name, tensor
+        trace("wrap_export.stream_end", weights=len(self.exported), will_compare=training_modules is not None)
+        if training_modules is not None:
+            self.compare_with_training(training_modules)
+
+    def _explain_silence(self, reason: str) -> None:
+        """Warn once that the comparison produced no verdict: a guard that silently does nothing is the failure
+        this module exists to prevent, so the reason is reported at WARNING."""
+        if self._explained:
+            return
+        self._explained = True
+        logger.warning(
+            "quantized-layer audit, training vs export, produced no verdict (%s). engine=%s weights=%d. Training "
+            "vs export is unverified for this run; VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT=0 silences the audit entirely.",
+            reason,
+            self.engine or "?",
+            len(self.exported),
+        )
+
+    def _report(self, msg: str) -> None:
+        if self.mode == "raise":
+            raise RuntimeError(msg)
+        logger.warning(msg)
+
+    def compare_with_training(self, training_modules) -> Optional[list[str]]:
+        """Compare the training-side FP8 trace with the recorded export. ``None`` if it did not run."""
+        trace("compare_with_training", enabled=self.enabled, finished=self.finished, weights=len(self.exported))
+        if self.finished or not self.enabled:
+            return None
+        if not self.exported:
+            self._explain_silence("the weight sync streamed no weights through the audit")
+            return None
+        report = collect_train_fp8_report(training_modules)
+        if not report.active:
+            # Give up only after two distinct syncs left no FP8 trace, counted by wrap_export(), so a second
+            # comparison on the same sync cannot trip this before the first training step.
+            if report.transpose_cache_disabled or self.syncs_seen >= 2:
+                self.finished = True
+                cause = (
+                    "disable_parameter_transpose_cache=True: TE caches the FP8 weight only when mcore passes "
+                    "is_first_microbatch, which that flag turns off"
+                    if report.transpose_cache_disabled
+                    else "no TE module holds an FP8 weight workspace after a training step; check that "
+                    "override_transformer_config.fp8 is set on the model that ran, and that nothing other "
+                    "than offload_megatron_model_to_cpu clears module._fp8_workspaces"
+                )
+                self._explain_silence(
+                    f"no training-side FP8 trace on this rank: 0 of {len(report.seen_layers)} decoder layers "
+                    f"left an FP8 weight workspace. Cause: {cause}"
+                )
+                return None
+            logger.info(
+                "quantized-layer audit, training vs export: no FP8 trace yet on this rank (%d decoder layers seen, "
+                "%d weights recorded); expected before the first training step, will retry at the next sync",
+                len(report.seen_layers),
+                len(self.exported),
+            )
+            return None
+        problems, by_design = audit_train_vs_export(report, self.exported)
+        unjudged = unjudged_weights(self.exported)
+        self.finished = True
+        n_q, n_seen = len(report.quantized_layers), len(report.seen_layers)
+        if not problems:
+            logger.info(
+                "quantized-layer audit: training and the exported weights agree (%d of %d decoder layers on this "
+                "rank ran FP8 GEMMs; %d weights checked, %d kept in BF16 on the rollout by design%s)",
+                n_q,
+                n_seen,
+                len(self.exported) - by_design - len(unjudged),
+                by_design,
+                _unjudged_note(unjudged),
+            )
+            return []
+        self._report(
+            f"quantized-layer audit: training and the exported weights disagree on {len(problems)} weight(s) "
+            f"({n_q} of {n_seen} decoder layers on this rank ran FP8 GEMMs{_unjudged_note(unjudged)}):"
+            + _listing(problems)
+            + "\nThe trainer ran these layers in one precision and the rollout is served them in another. Fix with "
+            "rollout.quantization.ignore (rollout) or first_last_layers_bf16 / model wiring (training)."
+            + " VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT=raise turns this into an error, =0 silences it."
+        )
+        return problems

+"""Export vs engine: is each synced weight sent in the format of the engine parameter that receives it?
+
+This is the rollout half of the quantized-layer audit; ``verl.utils.quant_layer_audit`` holds the training
+half (training vs export). Each rollout engine runs it in its own processes, inside the loader that writes a
+weight sync, so it reads the very parameters the sync is about to write:
+
+- vLLM: the colocated worker extension (``verl.workers.rollout.vllm_rollout.utils``), with the name
+  resolution of ``verl.utils.vllm.vllm_sync_format_check``;
+- SGLang: the MXFP8/MXFP4 refit loader (``verl.utils.sglang.sglang_quant_utils.load_and_reprocess``),
+  with the name resolution of ``verl.utils.sglang.sglang_sync_format_check``.
+
+It compares quantized against high precision, not exact dtypes. A quantized weight (FP8, packed FP4) sent to a
+BF16 parameter, or a BF16 weight sent to a quantized one, would be cast into a buffer of the other format, and a
+quantized layer would never receive its scale. The trainer-side exporter and the engine read the same
+quantization config (``rollout.quantization``, or the checkpoint's own ``quantization_config``), so a
+disagreement means the two matched a module differently, for example an ``ignore`` entry one side reads as a
+prefix and the other as an exact name.
+
+What a sync sends follows that config, and the engine keeps the formats it was built with, so a later sync cannot
+disagree where the first one agreed. The check therefore runs on every bucket of the first weight sync, before
+the bucket is written, and reports its totals once when that sync finishes; a sync that does not finish is
+checked again in full.
+
+``VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT``, shared with the training half: ``warn`` (default) logs the disagreements and lets the
+sync go on, ``raise`` stops the sync before the bucket is written, ``0`` disables.
+"""
+

+
+from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
+from typing import Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.quant_layer_audit import audit_mode, logger

+# HF leaf names that can be linear weights: ``.weight``, compressed-tensors' packed FP4 ``.weight_packed``, and
+# the fused expert tensors transformers >= 5 writes without a suffix (``mlp.experts.gate_up_proj``).
+_CHECKED_LEAVES = ("weight", "weight_packed", "gate_up_proj", "down_proj")
+_HIGH_PRECISION = (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.float32)
+_OFF = ("0", "off", "false")

+ResolveParam = Callable[[torch.nn.Module, str], Optional[torch.Tensor]]

+
+def _format(dtype: torch.dtype) -> str:
+    return str(dtype).removeprefix("torch.")
+
+
+class SyncFormatCheck:
+    """Export vs engine for one engine model. It lives on the model, so each engine process keeps its own."""
+
+    _ATTR = "_verl_sync_format_check"
+
+    def __init__(self, engine: str, resolve_param: ResolveParam):
+        self.engine = engine
+        self.resolve_param = resolve_param
+        self.finished = False  # the first weight sync has been checked end to end
+        # totals of the sync being checked
+        self.checked = 0  # weights compared with the parameter that receives them
+        self.disagreeing = 0  # of those, sent in another format than the parameter's
+        self.unmapped = 0  # names that resolve onto no engine parameter: not judged
+        self._buckets = 0
+
+    @classmethod
+    def of(cls, model: torch.nn.Module, engine: str, resolve_param: ResolveParam) -> SyncFormatCheck:
+        """The check attached to ``model``, created on first use."""
+        check = model.__dict__.get(cls._ATTR)

+            model.__dict__[cls._ATTR] = check
+        return check

+    @property
+    def pending(self) -> bool:
+        return not self.finished and audit_mode() not in _OFF
+
+    def begin_sync(self) -> None:
+        """Start a weight sync. Totals left by a sync that did not finish are dropped: it is checked again in full."""
+        if self.finished:
+            return
+        self.checked = self.disagreeing = self.unmapped = self._buckets = 0

+    def check_bucket(self, model: torch.nn.Module, named_tensors: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> None:
+        """Report the bucket's weights sent in another format than the receiving parameter's. Call before writing."""
+        if not self.pending:
+            return
+        problems = []
+        for name, tensor in named_tensors:
+            if name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] not in _CHECKED_LEAVES:

+                )

+        self.disagreeing += len(problems)
+        if problems:
+            self._report(problems)
+
+    def end_sync(self) -> None:
+        """After the first finished sync: report the totals once and stop checking."""
+        if not self.pending or self._buckets == 0:
+            return
+        self.finished = True

+            "quantized-layer audit, export vs %s engine, first weight sync: %d weights checked, %d in a format other "
+            "than the receiving parameter's, %d names not mapped onto an engine parameter (not judged); later syncs "
+            "send the same formats and are not checked again",
+            self.engine,
+            self.checked,
+            self.disagreeing,
+            self.unmapped,
+        )
+
+    def _report(self, problems: list[str]) -> None:
+        msg = (
+            f"quantized-layer audit: the weight sync and the {self.engine} engine disagree on the format of "
+            f"{len(problems)} weight(s):\n  - "
+            + "\n  - ".join(problems[:_MAX_LISTED])
+            + (f"\n  - ... and {len(problems) - _MAX_LISTED} more" if len(problems) > _MAX_LISTED else "")
+            + "\nThe trainer-side exporter and the engine read the same quantization config (rollout.quantization, "
+            "or the checkpoint's own quantization_config) but matched these modules differently. Loading would cast "
+            "each weight into a parameter of the other format, and a quantized layer would never receive its scale. "
+            "Check rollout.quantization.ignore against docs/low_precision/qat.md (Quantized-layer audit)."
+        )
+        if audit_mode() == "raise":
+            raise RuntimeError(msg + " The sync is stopped before this bucket is written.")
+        logger.warning("%s The sync goes on; VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT=raise stops it here, =0 disables the check.", msg)

+sync, ``check_bucket`` before each bucket is loaded and ``end_sync`` after the kernel layouts are re-derived.

+"""

+from typing import Optional

+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.quant_sync_format_check import SyncFormatCheck

+# HF projections SGLang fuses into one module (the model's stacked_params_mapping, restated).
+_STACKED = {
+    "q_proj": "qkv_proj",
+    "k_proj": "qkv_proj",
+    "v_proj": "qkv_proj",
+    "gate_proj": "gate_up_proj",
+    "up_proj": "gate_up_proj",
+}
+_W2_LEAVES = ("down_proj", "w2")
+_PARAM_LEAVES = ("weight", "weight_packed")
+
+
+def resolve_sglang_param(model: torch.nn.Module, hf_name: str) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
+    """The SGLang parameter that receives HF weight ``hf_name``, or ``None`` when the name does not resolve.
+
+    Walks the module tree by name, trying the fused module name for projections SGLang stacks
+    (``q_proj`` -> ``qkv_proj``, ``gate_proj`` -> ``gate_up_proj``) and stopping at a fused-MoE block
+    (a module holding ``w13_weight``), where the remaining per-expert parts select ``w13`` or ``w2``.
+    A packed FP4 ``.weight_packed`` lands in the module's ``weight_packed``, or in ``weight`` on a layer
+    the engine keeps in BF16.
+    """
+    parts = hf_name.split(".")
+    leaf = parts[-1] if parts[-1] in _PARAM_LEAVES else None
+    module_path = parts[:-1] if leaf else parts
+    cur: object = model
+    for i, part in enumerate(module_path):
+        if hasattr(cur, "w13_weight"):
+            return cur.w2_weight if any(r in _W2_LEAVES for r in module_path[i:]) else cur.w13_weight
+        nxt = getattr(cur, part, None)
+        if nxt is None and part in _STACKED:
+            nxt = getattr(cur, _STACKED[part], None)
+        if nxt is None:
+            return None
+        cur = nxt
+    if hasattr(cur, "w13_weight"):
+        return cur.w2_weight if parts[-1] in _W2_LEAVES else cur.w13_weight
+    if isinstance(cur, torch.nn.Module):
+        for attr in ("weight_packed", "weight") if leaf == "weight_packed" else ("weight",):
+            param = getattr(cur, attr, None)
+            if isinstance(param, torch.Tensor):
+                return param
+        return None
+    return cur if isinstance(cur, torch.Tensor) else None
+
+

+    """The export-vs-engine check of an SGLang model."""
+    return SyncFormatCheck.of(model, "sglang", resolve_sglang_param)

+from typing import Any, Optional

+import torch

+from verl.utils.quant_sync_format_check import SyncFormatCheck

+def _vllm_receiving_module(model: torch.nn.Module, name: str) -> Optional[torch.nn.Module]:
+    """The vLLM module that receives HF weight ``name``, or ``None`` when the name does not resolve.
+
+    Applies the model's ``hf_to_vllm_mapper``, then its ``packed_modules_mapping`` for the last
+    module name (``q_proj`` -> ``qkv_proj``), and stops at a fused-MoE block, whose remaining
+    per-expert parts (``experts.3.gate_proj``) its own weight loader resolves.
+    """
+    mapper = getattr(model, "hf_to_vllm_mapper", None)
+    if mapper is not None:
+        mapped = mapper.apply_list([name])
+        if not mapped:
+            return None
+        name = mapped[0]
+    parts = name.split(".")
+    path = parts[:-1] if parts[-1] in ("weight", "weight_packed") else parts
+    packed = getattr(model, "packed_modules_mapping", None) or {}
+    owner = {sub: fused for fused, subs in packed.items() for sub in subs}
+    module = model
+    for i, part in enumerate(path):

+            break
+        child = getattr(module, part, None)

+            child = getattr(module, owner[part], None)
+        if not isinstance(child, torch.nn.Module):
+            return None
+        module = child
+    for holder in ("routed_experts", "base_layer"):  # the MoE weight holder; the layer under a LoRA wrapper
+        inner = getattr(module, holder, None)
+        if isinstance(inner, torch.nn.Module):
+            module = inner
+    return module
+
+
+def resolve_vllm_param(model: torch.nn.Module, hf_name: str) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
+    """The vLLM parameter that receives HF weight ``hf_name``, or ``None`` when the name does not resolve.
+
+    A linear layer receives ``.weight`` in its ``weight`` and compressed-tensors' packed FP4 ``.weight_packed``
+    in its ``weight_packed``; a layer the engine keeps in BF16 has only ``weight``, which then receives the
+    packed weight. A fused-MoE block receives every expert's gate and up projections in ``w13_weight`` and
+    its down projection in ``w2_weight``. Layers another pipeline stage owns are unresolved on this rank.
+    """
+    module = _vllm_receiving_module(model, hf_name)
+    if module is None or type(module).__name__ == "PPMissingLayer":
+        return None
+    if hasattr(module, "w13_weight"):
+        parts = hf_name.split(".")
+        expert_parts = parts[parts.index("experts") + 1 :] if "experts" in parts else parts
+        return module.w2_weight if any(p in ("down_proj", "w2") for p in expert_parts) else module.w13_weight
+    candidates = ("weight_packed", "weight") if hf_name.endswith(".weight_packed") else ("weight",)
+    for attr in candidates:
+        param = getattr(module, attr, None)
+        if isinstance(param, torch.Tensor):
+            return param
+    return None
+
+
+def vllm_sync_format_check(model: torch.nn.Module, quant_config: Any = None) -> Optional[SyncFormatCheck]:
+    """The export-vs-engine check of a vLLM model, or ``None`` when the engine quantizes what it receives.

+    if getattr(quant_config, "is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized", True) is False:
+        return None
+    return SyncFormatCheck.of(model, "vllm", resolve_vllm_param)
